topics.name: Whole numbers
subtopics: Revise commutative, associative and distributive properties; 0 as additive identity and 1 as multiplicative identity
Recognise the division property of 0: any number divided by 0 is undefined
Revise prime factors, LCM and HCF of numbers to at least 3-digit whole numbers by inspection or factorisation
Solve problems involving ratio, rate, sharing in a given ratio and increasing or decreasing a number in a given ratio
Financial contexts: profit, loss, discount, VAT, budgets, accounts, loans, simple interest, hire purchase and exchange rates

topics.name: Integers
subtopics: Revise counting, ordering and comparing integers; revise addition and subtraction with integers
Multiply and divide with integers; calculations with all four operations
Calculations involving squares, cubes, square roots and cube roots of integers
Commutative, associative and distributive properties of addition and multiplication for integers
Additive and multiplicative inverses for integers
Solve problems in contexts involving multiple operations with integers

topics.name: Common fractions
subtopics: Revise addition, subtraction and multiplication of common fractions and mixed numbers, and finding fractions of whole numbers
Divide whole numbers and common fractions by common fractions using reciprocal relationships
Calculate squares, cubes, square roots and cube roots of common fractions
Revise calculation techniques: converting mixed numbers, simplifying with multiples and factors, using equivalent fractions
Solve problems involving common fractions and mixed numbers (grouping, sharing, fractions of whole numbers)
Percentages: revise percentage of whole numbers, of part of a whole and increase or decrease; calculate amounts given a percentage increase or decrease
Revise equivalent forms between common fractions, decimal fractions and percentages

topics.name: Formal assessment: Assignment
subtopics: Assignment on whole numbers, integers and common fractions

topics.name: Decimal fractions
subtopics: Revise ordering, comparing and place value to at least 3 decimal places; rounding off to at least 2 decimal places
Multiply decimal fractions by decimal fractions (not limited to one decimal place)
Divide decimal fractions by decimal fractions
Calculate squares, cubes, square roots and cube roots of decimal fractions
Revise calculation techniques; estimate decimal places using place value; check with rounding and a calculator
Revise equivalent forms of common fractions, decimal fractions and percentages
Solve problems in context involving decimal fractions

topics.name: Numeric and geometric patterns
subtopics: Revise investigating and extending numeric and geometric patterns (diagrams, tables, learners' own creation; not limited to constant difference or ratio)
Extend to patterns represented algebraically
Describe and justify general rules for observed relationships in own words or in algebraic language

topics.name: Revision and formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Revision and test on all Term 1 topics

sba: Assignment: whole numbers, integers and common fractions

topics.name: Exponents
subtopics: Revise representing whole numbers in exponential form; compare and represent integers in exponential form
Compare and represent numbers in scientific notation, limited to positive exponents
Establish general laws of exponents: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a × t)^n = a^n × t^n, a^0 = 1
Recognise and use laws of operations with exponents and square and cube roots
Calculate squares, cubes, square roots and cube roots of integers and rational numbers
Solve problems in contexts involving numbers in exponential form

topics.name: Algebraic expressions
subtopics: Algebraic language: interpret rules in symbolic form; identify variables, constants, like and unlike terms, coefficients and exponents
Add and subtract like terms using commutative, associative and distributive laws and laws of exponents
Multiply integers and monomials by monomials, binomials and trinomials
Divide monomials, binomials and trinomials by integers or monomials; simplify expressions
Determine squares, cubes, square roots and cube roots of single algebraic terms or like terms
Determine the numerical value of algebraic expressions by substitution

topics.name: Algebraic equations
subtopics: Set up equations to describe problem situations; analyse and interpret equations that describe a situation
Solve equations by inspection
Determine numerical values by substitution; use substitution to generate tables of ordered pairs
Identify variables and constants in formulae and equations
Extend solving equations to using additive and multiplicative inverses and laws of exponents

topics.name: Functions and relationships
subtopics: Revise determining input values, output values or rules using flow diagrams, tables and formulae; extend to equations
Revise and extend equivalence of descriptions of the same relationship presented verbally, in flow diagrams, tables, formulae, number sentences and equations

topics.name: Graphs
subtopics: Analyse and interpret global graphs: linear or non-linear, constant, increasing or decreasing
Extend features to maximum or minimum and discrete or continuous
Draw global graphs from descriptions of a problem situation
Use tables or ordered pairs to plot points and draw graphs on the Cartesian plane

topics.name: Revision and formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Revision and test on all Term 1 and Term 2 topics

sba: Investigation: on any ONE of the Term 2 topics, administered before teaching it

topics.name: Data handling
subtopics: Collect data: pose questions on social, economic and environmental issues; select sources; distinguish samples and populations
Design and use simple questionnaires with multiple-choice responses
Organise and record data using tally marks, tables and stem-and-leaf displays; group data into intervals
Summarise data using measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and dispersion (range, extremes)
Probability: list possible outcomes of simple situations with equally likely outcomes and determine the probability of each
Predict relative frequency for a series of trials and compare relative frequency with probability

topics.name: Geometry of straight lines
subtopics: Recognise and describe pairs of angles formed by perpendicular lines, intersecting lines and parallel lines cut by a transversal
Solve geometric problems using the relationships between pairs of angles

topics.name: Geometry of 2D shapes
subtopics: Define triangles by sides and angles: equilateral, isosceles, right-angled
Investigate angles in triangles using accurately constructed figures: interior angle sum, angles of equilateral triangles, sides and base angles of isosceles triangles
Define quadrilaterals by sides and angles: parallelogram, rectangle, square, rhombus, trapezium, kite
Investigate the interior angle sum of quadrilaterals and the sides and opposite angles of parallelograms
Identify and describe the properties of congruent and similar shapes
Solve geometric problems involving unknown sides and angles in triangles and quadrilaterals

topics.name: Revision and formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Revision and test on all Term 3 topics

sba: Project: covers a combination of topics from Term 1 to Term 3; completed before the end of Term 3

topics.name: Theorem of Pythagoras
subtopics: Investigate the relationship between the sides of a right-angled triangle to develop the Theorem of Pythagoras
Determine whether a triangle is right-angled given the lengths of its three sides
Calculate a missing length in a right-angled triangle, leaving irrational answers in surd form

topics.name: Transformation geometry
subtopics: Transform points on a co-ordinate plane: reflection in the x-axis, y-axis or line y = x; translation within and across quadrants; rotation about a given point
Identify the transformation of a point given the co-ordinates of its image
Transform triangles on a co-ordinate plane (reflection, translation, rotation about the origin) and track vertex co-ordinates
Use proportion to describe the effect of enlargement or reduction on area and perimeter
Investigate the co-ordinates of vertices of figures enlarged or reduced by a given scale factor

topics.name: Area and perimeter of 2D shapes
subtopics: Use formulae for perimeter and area of squares, rectangles, triangles and circles
Calculate areas of polygons to at least 2 decimal places by decomposing into rectangles and triangles
Relationships between radius, diameter and circumference, and between radius and area of a circle; meaning of π
Solve problems with or without a calculator involving perimeter and area of polygons and circles
Convert between SI units: mm² ↔ cm² ↔ m² ↔ km²

topics.name: Surface area and volume of 3D objects
subtopics: Revise surface area, volume and capacity of cubes and rectangular prisms; extend to triangular prisms
Describe the interrelationship between surface area and volume
Solve problems with or without a calculator involving surface area, volume and capacity
Convert between SI units: mm² ↔ cm² ↔ m² ↔ km², mm³ ↔ cm³ ↔ m³, ml (cm³) ↔ l ↔ kl

topics.name: Revision and formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Revision and test on Term 1 to Term 4 topics
